findings.description: The diff replaces `.claude/protocols/citations.md` with a Session Continuity stub pointing to `reference/session-continuity.md`. That leaves the citation protocol path no longer containing citation rules, while other protocol text still treats `citations.md` as the citation-format source.
findings.failure_mode: Agents or validators that load `.claude/protocols/citations.md` for citation requirements will read session-continuity guidance instead, so citation enforcement can silently stop applying or apply the wrong protocol.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the word-for-word citation protocol at `.claude/protocols/citations.md`, or if the intent was to stub a moved citation protocol, point it to the correct citation reference file and keep the title/content aligned with citations rather than session continuity.

findings.description: The sprint acceptance criterion 'Replay A/B: no gold case loses recall' is unmet on its own pre-registered terms. The gate fixed before extra trials (pooled n=9 after >= before, per losing case) fails on all five losing cases (review-pr-02, review-pr-05, audit-pr-02, audit-pr-03, audit-pr-05). Missed-defect slots doubled from 5/144 to 10/144. The pre-registered remedy ('revert or retune the implicated change') was not applied; instead a post-hoc blind adjudication re-scored the misses, and even on that measure audit-pr-02 still loses (0.963 vs 1.000). The adjudication itself attributes the grader drops to citation-format changes in the after arm (paren swallowed into path, continuation citations `:776,807`, `head:468`), which means the instruction diet did change output format, not just grader luck. The ablation only clears the context_discipline include; the protocol stubs (this hunk and session-continuity), the CLAUDE.loa.md trim, and the constraints rationale rewrite remain un-bisected.
findings.failure_mode: Measured recall regression in the reviewing-code and auditing-security skills ships to every consumer of the framework; downstream parsers that rely on the citation format (grader, verdict-trailer tooling) see more unparseable citations. The gate was moved after the result was known.
findings.suggested_fix: Hold the merge until one of: (a) bisect the remaining suspects (protocol stubs vs CLAUDE.loa.md trim vs constraints rationales) with the same 6-trial protocol and revert the implicated move per the pre-registered remedy; or (b) obtain explicit human sign-off to amend the AC, land the grader fix (bd-ewrc) test-first, re-baseline, and re-run the five losing cases before COMPLETED. Do not let the post-hoc adjudicated measure replace the pre-registered one without that sign-off.

findings.description: The new protocol text fails open: 'when it is absent, assume `long`', and the report states every hook error path (yq missing, catalog miss, alias unresolved, sanitiser rejecting the model id) also resolves to `long`. `long` thresholds are 10x the `standard` ones (150,000-token session total). On a <=200K model such as claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, 150K of accumulated tool results plus system prompt and skills exceeds Claude Code's auto-compact trigger, so compaction fires before the protocol's STOP-and-synthesize point. That is exactly the information loss the 'Clear, Don't Compact' paradigm exists to prevent.
findings.failure_mode: Haiku 4.5 (or any <=200K catalog model) on a machine without yq, or any session where SessionStart hooks did not run (hooks disabled, hook-guard skip, missing .run/), silently operates under long-class thresholds and loses un-synthesized decisions to auto-compaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Invert the fail-safe direction: unknown or error -> `standard`; only an affirmative catalog lookup with context_window > 200000 (or LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=long) selects `long`. If the default must stay `long` for the Claude 5 majority, at minimum emit a visible warning line in `/loa` and the hook stderr when the class was chosen by fallback rather than lookup, and add a CC test for the yq-absent path on a 200K model.

findings.cross_file_justification: The protocol text in this hunk instructs agents to trust `.run/context-class`; that file is written by `.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-context-class.sh`, which the report says is registered behind hook-guard.sh with `once` and only on SessionStart.
findings.description: `.run/context-class` is computed once per session at SessionStart. Claude Code allows switching models mid-session via `/model`, and `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS` can change between prompts; neither re-fires SessionStart. The record therefore goes stale: a session that starts on a 1M model and switches to a 200K model keeps `long` thresholds for the rest of the session. Two concurrent sessions in the same checkout with different models also race on the single file, last writer wins.
findings.failure_mode: Agent reads a stale `long` record on a 200K model after a mid-session model switch and over-accumulates tool results (see DISS-002 failure mode).
findings.suggested_fix: Record the model id alongside the class in `.run/context-class` (or a sibling file) and have the context_discipline include tell the agent to re-derive when the current model differs; or re-run the hook from a UserPromptSubmit hook with a cheap model-id compare. Document the staleness window in tool-result-clearing.md if not fixed.

findings.cross_file_justification: The removed text states that `pre-compact-marker.sh` and `post-compact-reminder.sh` 'inject the recovery sequence' and point at this protocol; `/run sprint-plan` unattended recovery and `br sync --flush-only` at session end were specified only here.
findings.description: The stub drops operational instructions that are not reference material: (1) Phase 1 step 0 'Run mode first: if `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` has state RUNNING, resume sprints.current immediately, no interactive recovery, no confirmation', which the removed text says 'is what lets /run sprint-plan survive context compaction during unattended execution'; (2) 'Always run `br sync --flush-only` at session end'; (3) Fork Detection / ledger-wins rule. These are now outside the prompt budget behind a pointer. The report claims 'No enforcement text was removed' but these are behavioral directives, not rationales. Unless post-compact-reminder.sh, CLAUDE.loa.md, or the run-state-surface hook output carry the run-mode resume instruction verbatim, an agent recovering from compaction mid-run sees only the notes-guard table and may stop to ask for confirmation.
findings.failure_mode: Unattended `/run sprint-plan` stalls on a confirmation prompt after compaction, or ends a session without flushing beads, losing task state.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep the run-mode step 0 and the `br sync --flush-only` line in the stub (they are under 300 bytes), or verify and cite in the report that post-compact-reminder.sh / CLAUDE.loa.md emit them independently, with a test that greps the hook output for `sprint-plan-state.json` and `RUNNING`.

findings.cross_file_justification: The thresholds became class-dependent in this hunk, but the texts moved verbatim to `.claude/protocols/reference/trajectory-evaluation.md` and `.claude/protocols/reference/session-continuity.md` (and, per synthesis-checkpoint.md's link, `attention-budget.md`) still hardcode the old single-class numbers.
findings.description: The moved reference text still says 'apply Tool Result Clearing if result_count > 20 or tokens_estimated > 2000', 'delta_sync phase is logged at the 5,000-token accumulated threshold (see tool-result-clearing.md)', and 'Run Delta-Synthesis at the Yellow threshold (5,000 tokens)'. Under the `long` class the live protocol says 20,000 / 50,000. An agent that follows the stub's pointer gets contradictory numbers, and the delta_sync trajectory field `tokens: 5000` no longer describes when the sync actually fires.
findings.failure_mode: Agents and the reviewing-code trajectory audit disagree on when clearing and delta-sync were required; audit flags compliant long-class sessions as late, or agents on `long` clear at 2K anyway, negating the diet.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the hardcoded numbers in the moved reference files and attention-budget.md with 'the class threshold in tool-result-clearing.md' or with both class values; add the two reference files to the protocol-refs-resolve or a threshold-consistency test.

findings.description: The first hunk is labeled `a/.claude/protocols/citations.md` but its removed content is the Session Continuity Protocol and its replacement is the session-continuity stub, while the supplied full-file context for citations.md shows the intact Word-for-Word Citation Protocol (with only the trajectory-evaluation pointer repointed). One of the two inputs is wrong. If the diff path is accurate, the citations protocol (grounding ratio rule, negative grounding, self-audit) was overwritten with a stub; if the full file is accurate, the diff was mislabeled by the review harness and the real citations.md change is a one-line repoint.
findings.failure_mode: If the diff path is literal, the citation protocol that synthesis-checkpoint Step 1 and the grounding-check script depend on is gone from the live tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `git show --stat 41b783a1 -- .claude/protocols/citations.md .claude/protocols/session-continuity.md` and confirm citations.md changed by one line and session-continuity.md is the 438->10 line stub. Fix the review-harness path mapping if that is the cause.

findings.description: The stub says it 'keeps the old path and its anchors stable' but changes the Level 2 recovery recipe: the removed text (and therefore the moved reference file) defines Level 2 as `ck --hybrid "..." grimoires/loa/ --top-k 3 --jsonl` (~200-500 tokens), while the stub defines Level 2 as `notes-guard.sh read --file F --section <H>` with `--index`. The in-budget stub and the out-of-budget reference now disagree on what Level 2 is, and the stub relies on `--file`, `--section`, and `--index` flags whose existence in notes-guard.sh is not evidenced in the report.
findings.failure_mode: An agent following the stub runs a notes-guard.sh invocation that may be rejected if those flags do not exist; an agent following the reference runs ck instead; recovery behavior differs by which file was read.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `notes-guard.sh read --file --section --index` exist (and are covered by notes-template.bats); update the Level 2 row in reference/session-continuity.md to match the stub, or restore the ck recipe in the stub.
